- Model consistently underestimates true price movements, especially after sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment > 0.75 → forecast lags or undershoots).
- Forecast shows strong upward bias in early days of the 30-day horizon, then flattens or slightly overestimates later — suggest adjusting for mean reversion after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., sentiment < 0.5 or sudden drops), model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections — apply downward bias correction for sentiment < 0.6.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model overestimates continuation, leading to overshoot — reduce forecast slope after spike by 10–15%.
- Forecast tends to ignore recent history (last 3–5 days) when sentiment is high — incorporate sentiment-weighted moving average for last 7–10 days to correct lag.
- If sentiment is rising steadily, model underreacts — increase forecast slope by 5–10% for sentiment > 0.7.
- For sentiment < 0.4, forecast is too optimistic — apply 5–10% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence bias.
